one_liner: Opt-in CPython 3.14+ interpreter loop in which opcodes tail-call each other; 3-5% faster than computed-goto (Clang 19), 15-20% faster than switch dispatch (MSVC).
what_it_does: This is a build-time alternative to CPython's bytecode dispatch loop, not a separate runtime. Configuring with --with-tail-call-interp (or PCbuild\build.bat --tail-call-interp on Windows) compiles each bytecode handler from the same generated_cases.c.h as its own small C function. Behaviour, C API and ABI are unchanged; per What's New 3.14 only speed differs. It is opt-in on Unix in 3.14, and the official python.org Windows x86-64 binaries use it from 3.15.
how_it_is_fast: The opcode handlers become separate functions marked with the preserve_none calling convention, and each one ends with a guaranteed tail call (musttail) through a function-pointer table: a 'goto with arguments'. Frame, stack pointer, tstate, next_instr, the dispatch table and oparg are passed as arguments, so they stay in registers across dispatches. The compiler can then allocate registers and lay out code per handler, instead of struggling with one giant switch or computed-goto function. On Clang 19 this also sidesteps an LLVM 19 change that merges all computed-goto dispatch jumps into one shared indirect branch.
when_to_use: You build your own CPython 3.14+ with Clang 19+ on x86-64 or AArch64 and use PGO (the only configuration the docs say was validated)
Your platform's CPython is normally built with Clang (macOS/Xcode, FreeBSD, OpenBSD), where the computed-goto loop suffers from the LLVM 19 dispatch-merging regression
Windows x86-64 on 3.15+: the python.org binaries already use it; when building yourself, VS 2026 (MSVC 18, v145) gives 15-20% over the switch-case loop
You want a few percent on interpreter-bound pure-Python code without any compatibility cost; in the gist, numeric loops (scimark_*) and unpack_sequence gained most
when_not_to_use: Linux distribution Python built with GCC: against GCC or clang-18 computed-goto builds the gain measured by Nelson Elhage was 1.00-1.03x (blog known from a search snippet only)
Builds without PGO: the issue says the speedup is mediocre without it
Python 3.13 or older, or compilers lacking both musttail and preserve_none (main's ceval_macros.h stops the build with #error; 3.14 rejects MSVC entirely)

Builds with frame pointers (default in 3.15 per PEP 831) or other per-function hardening: issue #154124 measures 2.7% of geomean lost to frame pointers in the tail-calling interpreter vs 1.5% in the computed-goto one (i7-12700H, Clang 22); a fix is proposed but open
You need multi-x speedups: PyPy, Cython, mypyc or Codon are in a different league; the 3.15 JIT adds a further 11-12% over this interpreter on AArch64 macOS

integration.form: build option of the CPython interpreter (./configure --with-tail-call-interp; PCbuild\build.bat --tail-call-interp)
integration.dependencies: none beyond CPython's normal build; needs a C compiler with both musttail and preserve_none
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.14+; Clang 19+ (x86-64, AArch64) on Unix; Visual Studio 2026 / MSVC 18 (PlatformToolset v145, _MSC_VER >= 1950) on Windows for 3.15+; GCC only once it provides preserve_none (What's New 3.14 says a future GCC is expected to)
integration.platforms: x86-64 and AArch64 (Linux, macOS); Windows x86-64 with MSVC 18 from 3.15; python-build-standalone enables it for 3.14+ builds compiled with clang
integration.thread_safety: Same as the regular interpreter (GIL or free-threaded build); a VS 2026 free-threaded build failure (#144549) was fixed in Feb 2026
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — no Python-visible, C-API or ABI change, but you must rebuild CPython with a supported compiler and PGO, or use a distribution that enables it (python.org Windows x64 3.15, python-build-standalone 3.14+ clang builds)

gotchas: The headline numbers depend on the baseline. The issue's original 10% geomean (gist: 1.10x, best 1.46x on scimark_sor) came from comparing against a Clang 19 computed-goto build slowed by an LLVM 19 bug, and the authors withdrew it. What's New still names 'Python 3.14 built with Clang 19' as the baseline for its 3-5%, while issue #158283 (Sep 2026) shows plain Clang 19 computed-goto builds remain 7.7% slower than GCC 13 on Linux x86-64. It is not documented whether the 3-5% was measured against a repaired baseline.

The Windows 15-20% (Ryzen 7 5800X, MSVC 18.1.1) is measured against the switch-case loop, because MSVC has no computed gotos. It is not comparable to the clang figures, where the baseline is computed-goto dispatch.

Each opcode handler is a real function, so per-function prologue features (frame pointers, CET/BTI shadow stacks) cost more here than in a single-function loop (#154124). Profilers and debuggers show per-opcode _TAIL_CALL_* frames instead of _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault.

Enabling the flag on an unsupported toolchain is a trap: a 3.14.0rc2 build with GCC 14, PGO and --with-tail-call-interp hit 'RecursionError: Stack overflow (used 8161 kB)' during the PGO step (#138215, closed not planned). The pyconfig.h macro was renamed from Py_TAIL_CALL_INTERP (3.14) to _Py_TAIL_CALL_INTERP (main), which matters for build-detection scripts.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you must stay on upstream CPython with full C-extension and ABI compatibility and accept single-digit gains. Pyston gives more but is frozen at CPython 3.8. PyPy, GraalPy, Cython, mypyc and Codon can give multi-x speedups but mean a different runtime or a compile step. It stacks with them rather than replacing them.
verified_claims_summary: Ken Jin's first-party run (pyperformance, clang-19 with ThinLTO and PGO, AMD64 Ubuntu 22.04, CPU model not given) compared tail-call commit 465467f47553 with main 2228e92da31c from the same day. It found 1.10x geomean (52 faster, 1 slower: unpickle_list 1.02x; 8 not significant), later corrected to 3-5% after the LLVM 19 baseline regression was found. An independent run by Nelson Elhage (snippet only) found 1.03x on an i5-13500 and 1.00x on an Apple M1 against clang-18. Separately, What's New 3.15 reports 15-20% on Windows x86-64 with MSVC 18 against the switch-case loop on a Ryzen 7 5800X.
status_note: Actively maintained in upstream CPython (Python-2.0 licence, commits daily as of 2026-10-06). It is opt-in on Unix but already shipped in python.org Windows x64 3.15 binaries and in python-build-standalone clang builds for 3.14+, so the realistic decision is which CPython build to use, not whether to adopt a library.
sources_read: WebSearch: 'Python 3.14 tail-calling interpreter vs GCC computed goto build benchmark nelhage clang 18' (blog.nelhage.com/post/cpython-tail-call snippet only; blog blocked)
